thread:
marie: Quick q — seeing a lot more interruption churn on EU spot pools this morning. Scale-out is aggressive, then we get waves of evictions and lots of cold starts. Thinking about an adaptive preemptible throttle + warmup probe to smooth surge and reduce wasted token cost. anyone experimented with an approach like that?

thomas: How bad are we talking? interruption rate / scale events per hour?

marie: ~12% interruption prob on m-p4 pools during 06:00-10:00 UTC, ~4 scale events / min at peak, tail latency spikes to 800ms for small requests because new nodes haven't warmed KV caches. Cost leak from repeated warmups looks non-trivial.

anya: Oof. We saw similar in NA last year. Two levers that worked for us: 1) short-term surge throttle based on smoothed interruption probability; 2) a warmup probe that marks instances as "ready" only after KV warm fraction > 0.6.

leo: Agree. Also limit concurrent scale-outs: if there are >X pending scale tasks, push cooldowns to avoid thundering. We added a soft cap of 8 concurrent node joins per fleet and it cut churn.

marie: Thinking of a policy that: compute interruption_prob = EWMA(spot_evictions, 10m), then allowed_surge = base_surge * (1 - interruption_prob * alpha). If allowed_surge < 1 -> throttle additional scale-outs and prefer warm standby.

thomas: Sounds solid. What's alpha? and what's the fallback when warm standby depleted?

marie: alpha = 0.8 as a starting point. Fallback = spill to reserved on-demand pool OR route lower-priority requests to cheaper model quantized variant.

anya: Can you paste config we could trial? small YAML plz.

marie: Sure — draft config: 
```
autoscaler: 
  mode: mixed
  reserved_capacity_fraction: 0.15
  base_surge: 2.0
  cooldown_seconds: 240
  warmup_probe_seconds: 60
  kv_warm_threshold: 0.6
  interruption_ewma_window_seconds: 600
  interruption_alpha: 0.8
  concurrent_join_soft_cap: 8
  surge_throttle_policy: "allowed_surge = base_surge * (1 - interruption_prob * interruption_alpha)"
```

leo: Nice. Can we add a fast path for very high-priority traffic to bypass throttle but with stricter cost accounting? e.g., route X% critical -> on-demand pool only.

marie: Yup, add route-level priority flag. We'll also emit metrics: spot_interruption_prob, allowed_surge, kv_warm_fraction, pending_joins_count so we can visualize.

infra-bot: deploy-preview created for branch "adaptive-preemptible-throttle" — CI passed.

thomas: Two quick concerns: 1) cooldown too long could increase latency if demand jumps, 2) warmup_probe 60s may be too conservative for small models. Maybe make warmup_probe per-model (30s for <2B params).

anya: Good call. Make warmup_probe adaptive: min(60s, model_size_factor * 10s). Also add grace TTL for cached KV entries so warm standby has better hit rate.

marie: Action items:
- roll out config to canary fleet in eu-west-1 with on-demand fallback (marie)
- dashboards for spot_interruption_prob, allowed_surge, pending_joins_count (anya)
- per-model warmup tuning + model_size_factor heuristic (thomas)

leo: I'll throttle the autoscaler controller to honor concurrent_join_soft_cap in the next patch.

marie: If this reduces churn by half we're in good shape cost-wise. Will report back after 2h canary window. :crossed_fingers:

infra-bot: canary started (fleet eu-west-1-canary). monitoring.link/dashboard/abcd

thomas: 👍 keep an eye on token-cost-per-request metric as well (we should see warmup-related token overhead drop).

marie: Thanks all — ping me if you see regressions.
